title: Edit mode still slow on large documents after 1.9.2: commit round trip and editor open
body:
Follow-up to #420 (fixed in v1.9.2). Edit mode on large documents is faster in 1.9.2, but still felt as slow on one document: `08-research-plan-implement.md` of the agentic-coding white paper (~1,100 lines, 238 table rows, 16 figures, ~4,350 DOM nodes in the preview). This issue holds a new measurement campaign on that document only.

## Setup

- VS Code 1.147 (Electron 43), macOS, isolated `--user-data-dir` / `--extensions-dir`, driven over CDP (`--remote-debugging-port`, `--inspect-extensions`).
- Extension 1.9.2 with `preview.js`, `extension.js` and `renderWorker.js` rebuilt **unminified with source maps** from the 1.9.2 tag, so every cost below maps to a source line.
- Three probes at once: browser-level trace (all renderers, forced style/layout with JS stacks), JS CPU profile of the webview, JS CPU profile of the extension host and of the render worker thread.

## Summary

| Interaction | 1.9.2 in real VS Code | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Typing in an open block editor | p50 33 ms (= 2 frames), ~3.5 ms JS + ~5 small forced layouts per key | fine |
| Hover (edit toolbar, menus, blocks) | 50–96 ms p50 | mostly paint + VS Code core, see below |
| **Open a block editor** (click a paragraph) | **~350–390 ms wall**, 190 ms webview JS | **slow** |
| **Commit an edit** (Cmd+Enter) → new version shown | **~660–680 ms** warm, **~1,750 ms** for the first commit after opening the preview | **slowest — this is what is felt** |

The headless page bench used for #420 shows 1.9.1 ≈ 1.9.2 except typing (halved): it does not reproduce the felt slowness, because the commit round trip goes through the extension host and the render worker.

## 1. Commit round trip (Cmd+Enter): ~670 ms, up to 1.75 s

Timeline of one warm commit (extension host + worker + webview profiles):

| Step | Time | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Edit applied to the document, notification sent | ~30 ms | `handleEditSave` → `drainActiveBlockEdit` → `applyEdits` |
| **Adaptive debounce before the render starts** | **164–187 ms** (570 ms after the first build) | `BuildQueue.currentDebounceMs()` (`src/core/render/buildQueue.ts:175`) |
| MyST render in the worker | ~90 ms | `renderMyst` (`mystParse` 30 ms, `mystToHtml` 27 ms) |
| Content patch planning on the host | ~65 ms | `planContentPatch` → `analyze` + `shellOf`: **parse5 parses the HTML twice** (`src/core/preview/contentPatch.ts:74/156`) |
| Properties table patch | ~20 ms | `deferWhileEditing` → `patchPropertiesTable` → `replacePropertiesTableHtml`: **a third parse5 parse** (`src/core/frontmatter/propertiesTable.ts:324`) |
| IPC serialization | ~25 ms | `writeChannelMessage` |
| **Webview: apply the patch** | **~300 ms** JS (358 ms with GC) | see below |

Logged queue values (instrumented `extension.js`):
```
request debounce=40    built renderMs=285   (first build after opening)
request debounce=570   built renderMs=82    ← first commit waits 570 ms
request debounce=164   built renderMs=93
request debounce=187   built renderMs=89
```

**Debounce.** The adaptive wait (2 × last render, 40..1000 ms) is meant for typing in the text editor. An explicit commit from the preview is a single, final change: waiting before it renders is pure latency. The first render after opening (285 ms, cold JIT) also sets a 570 ms wait for the next one.

**Webview patch (~300 ms JS)**, source-mapped inclusive times under `contentPatch.ts:28`:

| Cost | ms | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `tableRowMove.refresh` → `position` | **~100** (97 self) + forced style **75–79** + layout **23** | `src/page/features/tableRowMove.ts:491-493` |
| `contentMorph.replace` (`replaceChildren`, `remove`) | ~80 | `src/page/modules/contentMorph.ts:158` |
| `closeBlockEdit` | 59, forced style 37 | `src/page/features/blockEditor.ts:95` |
| `scrollCore.measure` / `parseMappings` / `maxScrollTop` | ~27 + forced style 16 | `src/page/features/scrollCore.ts:116/177/337` |
| `firstClearance` `geometry` | forced style 17 | `src/page/modules/firstClearance.ts:74` |
| `refreshStickyHeadingPosition` | forced style 15 | `src/page/features/stickyHeadings.ts:56` |
| `selectBlocksNow` | forced style 14 | `src/page/features/blockSelectionView.ts:123` |

Seven full-document forced style recalcs (13–79 ms each) run in one task, each one invalidated again by the writes of the previous step. `tableRowMove.position` runs synchronously from `applyEditMode` during the patch (not in its rAF) and reads `getBoundingClientRect` on every row of every table (238 rows here) right after the patch dirtied the whole tree.

## 2. Opening a block editor: ~350–390 ms

Extension host side is negligible (3 ms, `handleEditOpen`). All the cost is in the webview: 190 ms JS, dominated by forced full-document style recalcs interleaved with writes:

| Forced recalc caller | Style | Layout |
|---|---|---|
| `beginEditAnchor` (`src/page/features/scrollCore.ts:247`) | 20–26 ms | 3–5 ms |
| `firstClearance` `geometry` (`src/page/modules/firstClearance.ts:74`) | 18–25 ms | 1–2 ms |
| `syncPaletteSticky` (`src/page/features/editorChrome.ts:158`) | 17–22 ms | 1–4 ms |
| `resizeTextarea` ×2 (`src/page/features/blockSourceEditor.ts:144`) | 17–20 ms | 5–11 ms |
| `clickCaretContext` (`src/page/features/editMode.ts:95`) | 12 ms | — |

Plus `measureLineTops` / `measure` (`scrollCore.ts:89/118/337`) ~32 ms, `getBoundingClientRect` 89 ms self in total. The writes between the reads include `data-sphinx-preview-block-editing` on `document.documentElement` (`blockEditor.ts` ~318), which invalidates the style of the whole document.

## 3. Hover: 50–96 ms, mostly not ours

Our hover JS is negligible (14 ms for 30 moves on the edit toolbar). The webview renderer spends the time in `BeginMainFrame` → PrePaint (69 ms / 30 moves) and paint of the large DOM (~6 ms per move). The workbench renderer adds, on every mouse move forwarded by the webview (`did-mouse-move`), VS Code's `workbench.sash.autoHideGrippers` handler (a `removeAttribute` on a root element → 1–3 ms style recalc) plus GC. That part is VS Code core.

## Candidate fixes (by expected gain)

1. **Commit renders without debounce**: a commit from the preview requests the build with a 0 ms wait (or a `flush` on the queue); keep the adaptive wait for text-editor typing. Saves ~170 ms per commit, ~570 ms on the first one. Optionally do not count the first (cold) build in `lastBuildMs`.
2. **Table handles off the patch path**: `tableRowMove` positions its handles in its own rAF (as `schedulePosition` already does) instead of synchronously in `applyEditMode`/`initializeContent`; only tables near the viewport, or handles positioned on hover. Saves ~100–200 ms per commit.
3. **One read phase after the patch and on open**: batch all writes (editor close/open, root attributes, handle styles) first, then let `closeBlockEdit`, `scrollCore.measure`, `firstClearance`, `stickyHeadings`, `blockSelectionView`, `beginEditAnchor`, `syncPaletteSticky`, `resizeTextarea` read in one rAF. Replace the `documentElement` attribute toggle with a scoped class/attribute so it does not invalidate every element. Target: 1 forced recalc instead of 5–7 (~80–150 ms saved on each).
4. **Parse the rendered HTML once on the host**: share the parse5 tree between `analyze`, `shellOf` and the properties-table patch (~40–50 ms per commit).
5. Paint on hover: `contain: layout paint` / `content-visibility` on top-level blocks (careful with rect-based scroll sync), lazy insert bars.

Expected result for 1–4: commit ~670 ms → ~250 ms, open ~370 ms → ~200 ms.
